report.tagline: Software that lets anyone set up an online store, take payments and sell everywhere, from a website to Instagram, shops and AI chatbots.
report.simpleSummary: Shopify lets a business build its own online store without coding. You pick a theme, add products, and Shopify handles checkout, payments, shipping labels and taxes. Shops pay a monthly plan fee, and Shopify takes a small cut of each card payment. Apps from other developers add extras, and an AI helper called Sidekick can run tasks for you.

overview.whatItDoes: Shopify gives merchants the tools to sell online and in person: a store builder, checkout (Shop Pay), payments, point-of-sale hardware, shipping, a consumer app (Shop), loans (Shopify Capital) and an app store. It powers small sellers and big brands like Gymshark and Mattel. It makes money from subscriptions and, mostly, from taking a cut of merchant sales.
howItWorks: A merchant signs up for a free trial, picks a theme and adds products.
They choose a plan: Basic, Grow, Advanced or Plus for large brands.
Customers pay through Shopify Checkout and Shop Pay; Shopify Payments takes a percentage per card payment.
Merchants add apps from the Shopify App Store for reviews, email, subscriptions and more.
Sidekick, an AI assistant, answers questions and builds automations in the admin.
Products can be sold on Instagram, TikTok, Google, Amazon and AI agents like ChatGPT from one place.
overview.valueProposition: For merchants: own your brand and customers, start fast, and grow from a side hustle to a big brand on one platform. For Shopify: earn more as merchants sell more.

businessModel.summary: Shopify earns from monthly plans (subscription solutions) and from a cut of merchant sales through payments, shipping, loans and other services (merchant solutions, 78% of revenue).

$836 million in Q3 2026: plan fees, apps, themes and domains.
Enterprise plans from about $2,300 a month.
Cut of sales from app developers above a threshold.

businessModel.pricing: US list prices: Basic about $39 a month ($29 billed yearly), Grow about $105 ($79 yearly), Advanced about $399 ($299 yearly), Plus from about $2,300 a month. Card rates on Basic online around 2.9% plus 30 cents. Extra fee if a merchant uses another payment provider.
costDrivers: R&D, including AI ($497 million in Q3)
businessModel.unitEconomics: A merchant on Basic selling $10,000 a month pays $39 in fees and about $320 in card fees. Shopify keeps most of the $39 and about $50 to $80 of the card fees after paying card networks. That is roughly $1,000 to $1,400 a year in gross profit from one small merchant. Shopify's overall take rate is about 3.1% of GMV ($3.74 billion revenue on $119 billion GMV).

howTheyGetUsers: Free trials and low starting price
Point of sale for physical shops
whatBringsUsersBack: Shop Pay that shoppers already use
growth.moat: Shopify's moat is its ecosystem: thousands of apps, agencies and developers, plus Shop Pay saved by over 400 million shoppers. Once a business runs on Shopify, switching means rebuilding store, apps and payments.
